sentences.text:
This writ petition has been filed, seeking the following reliefs:-
i. Issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate order directing the 6th respondent to release an amount of Rs.85,13,227/- from the amounts awarded as per Exhibit P2 and P3 to the 3rd respondent to be credited towards the SGST liability of the petitioner as the full and final settlement of the same.

ii. Issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate order directing the 3rd respondent to accept the amounts released by the 6th respondent as full and final payment towards the SGST liability of the petitioner by giving the petitioner the benefit of Exhibit P1 amnesty scheme of the Government.

Sulphi S vs State Of Kerala on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116925405/
2 iii.

iv. Issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate order directing the 4th respondent to consider and dispose Exhibit P11 expeditiously.
2.
Ext .P1 Amnesty Scheme has now been replaced by a new Amnesty Scheme introduced in the year 2024 by the provisions of the Kerala Finance Act, 2024.
The new Scheme is on record as Ext.P12.
The last date for filing application in terms of the provisions contained in Ext.P12 Scheme is 29.09.2024.

A reading WP(C) NO. 38477 OF 2023 2024:KER:70209 of the pleadings in the writ petition will indicate that certain amounts have been determined as due to the petitioner on account of compensation for acquisition of land for the purposes of Development of the National Highway.

According to the petitioner, a sum of Rs.87,36,055/- which is to be paid to the petitioner on account of compensation for land acquisition as per Exts.P2 and P3 awards can be directed to be paid over to the Sales Tax Department so that the petitioner can file an application for settlement under the Amnesty Scheme of 2024.
3.

The learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that though applications produced as Exts.P13 to P19 have already been filed, they are not being processed as the Amnesty Scheme requires the deposit of at least 30% of the amount (to be paid) along with the application.
4. Heard the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents.

The learned Special Government Pleader would submit that, on enquiries it is learnt that the amount of compensation payable to the petitioner in terms of Exts.P2 and P3 Awards have not been so paid on account of the fact that the petitioner has not produced the necessary documents before the 5th respondent.

It is also submitted that the applications WP(C) NO. 38477 OF 2023 2024:KER:70209 now produced as Exts.P13 to P19 have been rejected on account of the fact that the orders showing the arrear amounts have not been produced and also on account of the fact that the applications were not accompanied by upfront payment as contemplated by the provisions of the Scheme.

However, he submits that the Taxes Department has no objection in adjusting any amount that may be released by the 5th respondent under Exts.P2 and P3 awards against the amounts payable by the petitioner in terms of the Amnesty Scheme.

It is submitted that, if those amounts were to be received and if the petitioner were to make fresh applications along with necessary documents before 29.09.2024, the claim of the petitioner can be considered in accordance with the terms of the Amnesty Scheme.

Having heard the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner and the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents, this writ petition will stand disposed of with the following directions:-
(i) The 5th respondent shall release the amounts payable to the petitioner in terms of Exts.P2 and P3 awards directly to the account to be intimated by the Sales Tax Officer (Arrear Recovery), State Goods and Services Tax Department, Tax WP(C) NO. 38477 OF 2023 2024:KER:70209 Payer Services Circle, Alappuzha.
